name: Uma Gupta

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary shift like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and operate a soap-bottle filling and capping line. My vocational certificate covered safe stops and fill levels, and I like finding one loose cap before a whole pallet leaks. Washing dried soap off the belt after a bad run is the part nobody volunteers for.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How are things at home, and do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner repairs buses. We have two school-age children, a mortgage and four months of expenses saved. The filling job pays about the usual operator rate and there are some similar plants nearby. I use AI every day to sort reject logs, then check the suggested pattern against real bottles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the filling crew the AI spreadsheet has been useful for sorting rejected soap bottles, but the bottle still needs a proper cap. If the bigger promise fizzles, we keep checking actual leaks. Nobody buys a bottle because the report looks tidy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My operator wage is about average, my partner repairs buses, and we have four months of expenses saved. With two school-age children and a mortgage I still watch the bills, but both jobs have been steady. There are some similar packing plants nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep setting the soap-bottle filler and pulling three capped samples after each changeover. I already use AI every day to organise the reject log, and I'll keep comparing its pattern with the actual bottles. I'll put a new amount from each full pay month into our repair reserve after bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the line and our current money. I would like the spreadsheet to save some counting, but it will not judge a leaking cap for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the reject log help you find?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week the reject log put the leaks near the middle of the shift. I watched the capper at that time and found a loose guide rail. A spreadsheet can point me to the minute; my hands still have to tighten the capper guide rail.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why add to the repair reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our washing machine is noisy and the children have school costs coming. We'd use any new reserve deposits for a repair rather than assume the current four months can cover every bill. I check the amount after payday, not before it.

say: An **AI reject log** can point to leaks but cannot tighten a loose capper rail.
The crew should keep **testing soap bottles** even if the larger AI promise fades.
think: Our **four-month reserve** and two steady wages make this mild case manageable.
The **mortgage** and children's costs still need regular attention.
do: **Keep** setting the filler and testing capped samples each changeover.
**Add** new money from full pay months to the repair reserve after bills.
feel: **Calm** about current work and household money.
S0.quote: A spreadsheet can point me to the minute; my hands still have to tighten the capper guide rail.
fieldNote: Uma **uses AI daily** on a reject log and checks patterns against actual bottles.
New **reserve deposits** come from future full wages after bills; current savings are a separate buffer.

steps.text: Keep filling soap bottles and test capped samples each changeover
Save new money from full wages into repair reserve after bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI may plan packing orders and write inspection notes long before a robot can handle every sticky bottle. I want a clear trial on our line before a faster target becomes a new rule. Results should include leaks, not just bottles per hour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I like learning a useful tool, and our four months saved gives some room. Yet a new schedule might combine two filling shifts and put my regular hours at risk. My partner's bus-repair wage would help, but we still pay a mortgage and school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the line manager for last month's paid hours and cap-leak rate before the new target. If the plant offers a paid guarded trial on its new capper controls with a trainer, I'll take the place and learn the controls. I'll also practise a new AI chart on anonymised reject data after my shift, verifying it against the bottle log.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible shorter roster, but curious about the controls. I can test a new capper; I cannot test a missing wage after it is gone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the new capper control?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd set a cap too loose on a training bottle and see whether the new control stops it. A trainer would have to show the safe stop and keep hands clear of the belt. I would not learn this on live production alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the rota tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the posted base shifts, not a promise of overtime. If one full shift disappears, my partner and I would work out the mortgage gap before I agreed to a new rota. The leak rate matters too.

say: **AI planning** may change packing schedules before robots can handle every bottle.
I want a **guarded trial** that measures leaks as well as line speed.
think: A merged **filling roster** could reduce my regular hours.
Our **four-month buffer** helps, but a mortgage still needs full pay.
do: **Compare** actual base hours and leak rates before accepting a new target.
**Learn** new capper controls if a paid trainer-led guarded trial is offered.
**Practise** a fresh AI chart on anonymised reject data and verify it.
feel: **Anxious** about possible paid-hour loss with control over testing.
S1.quote: I can test a new capper; I cannot test a missing wage after it is gone.
fieldNote: Her **adaptive style** leads to an offered paid guarded control trial and a new AI reject chart.
She compares **base wages** and leak rates before accepting a target that might combine shifts.

steps.text: Compare paid base shifts and leak rate before accepting target
Learn capper controls if paid guarded trainer-led trial offered
Practise new AI reject chart on anonymised data and verify results

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew thinking AI by 2028 could order every bottle and plan our rota, then capable robots around 2031 could fill, cap and inspect them. We should ask for a staffing date in writing, not guess from a supplier's visit. I would keep checking what actually gets installed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 48 when robots reach the hands-on line. I think a big part of our packing crew could go, including my shift, and bus repairs might also change as robots spread. Four months saved would give us breathing space, not another steady wage. I have lain awake working out what happens if both rotas shrink.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll ask the manager for the written robot plan and any paid quality roles. If the plant offers a funded, paid-time qualification in leak testing with a real guarded practice place, I'll enrol. If my filling hours are cut, I'll apply for posted safe local packing jobs at enough regular base pay and workable school hours; after qualifying, I'll also apply for posted local leak-testing jobs under those same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. A robot can be bought in a week; a second household wage cannot be found on a purchase order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would leak-testing training teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The practical test should include a bottle with a loose cap and one with a hairline crack. I'd stop the belt, measure the leak and record the failed batch while a trainer checks me. I would need that practice on paid time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which packing job would you apply to?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The fallback packing job must be actually posted nearby and have a safe shift that covers school pickup. I would compare the base rate with our mortgage and bus-repair wage, not assume overtime. If that rate falls short, I keep searching.

say: **2028 thinking AI** could plan bottles before capable robots fill and cap around 2031.
We need a **written staffing date** before trusting supplier hints.
think: At **48**, I could lose a large part of my packing wage.
Four months saved cannot replace **two shrinking rotas** for long.
do: **Ask** manager for written robot and paid quality-role plans.
**Enrol** if funded paid guarded leak-testing qualification offered.
**Apply** for posted safe local packing or qualified testing work if cut and pay fits.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected large loss and sleepless household-wage calculations.
S2.quote: A robot can be bought in a week; a second household wage cannot be found on a purchase order.
fieldNote: She expects **substantial crew cuts** and has lost sleep over simultaneous household-hour risk.
The **packing fallback** and qualified testing application require actual local posts, safe shifts, sufficient base pay and school-compatible hours.

steps.text: Ask manager for written robot staffing and paid quality-role plans
Enrol in leak testing if funded paid guarded qualification place offered
Apply for posted safe local packing if hours cut, base pay and school hours fit
Apply for posted safe local leak testing if qualified, hours cut, pay and school hours fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2031 may plan soap orders, and capable robots around 2034 could handle the bottles. Five years can pay for real training if the plant starts while we still have shifts. A course seat matters more than a glossy video.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 51 when physical robots arrive. We could grow our reserve if both wages stay full, though a qualification might still lead nowhere if the plants stop hiring. I want to compare a real posting with our mortgage before leaving a job that pays today.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll put new money from each offered paid overtime shift into our repair and job-gap reserve. I'll ask the plant for the exact funded fees, paid release and guarded practice place for a capper-maintenance certificate. If a place is offered, I'll enrol; after qualifying, if filling hours fall, I'll apply for posted safe local maintenance openings with base pay enough for our bills and school-compatible shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the later line change, though five years lets me check each step. I can learn a capper while still earning from one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the maintenance certificate teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd need to isolate the capper, replace a worn guide and run a test bottle under the trainer's eye. The plant should pay for those practice hours. A capper-maintenance certificate without a safe stop is paper, not a job skill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a posting worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I won't leave the filling line for a maintenance title alone. The posting must show regular base pay, a real local site and shifts we can cover around the children. My partner and I would compare the offer after bills.

say: **2031 thinking AI** could plan orders before robots handle bottles around 2034.
Five years should fund **real course seats** while operators still earn.
think: At **51**, I may still need filling wages for the mortgage.
A qualification helps only if **local plants** post safe paid work.
do: **Save** new wages from offered overtime shifts after bills.
**Enrol** in capper maintenance if fees, paid release and guarded place covered.
**Apply** for posted safe local maintenance if qualified, hours cut and pay sufficient.
feel: **Anxious** about later income risk with time to verify offers.
S3.quote: A capper-maintenance certificate without a safe stop is paper, not a job skill.
fieldNote: Her **new savings** depend on offered paid overtime, distinct from the existing four-month reserve.
The **maintenance application** follows qualification and hour cuts, and needs a safe local post with adequate base pay and school hours.

steps.text: Save new money from offered paid overtime after bills
Enrol in capper maintenance if funded paid guarded place offered
Apply for posted safe local maintenance if qualified, hours cut, base pay and school hours fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI in 2036 might plan every packing order, with capable robots around 2039 on the filling line. A decade is enough to prepare if we keep checking real wages and courses. It does not make every supplier brochure true.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 56 when robots do the hands-on filling. The children may be grown, but I cannot assume the mortgage is gone. Four months saved now and two regular wages give us room to plan, though I still need work after 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the filler job and add new savings from full pay months after bills. I'll ask the local equipment supplier for a written paid trainer place in machine setup, including guarded practice and a recognized qualification. If an actual funded place is offered, I'll take it; after qualifying, if filling hours shrink, I'll apply to posted safe local setup jobs only if regular pay and travel time fit our household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far-off line, but the current wage is steady. I can make one move at a time when a real place appears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the supplier need to teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the supplier whether the training includes a live line with the power isolated and a person to check my work. I can already read a manual with AI, but I need hands-on setup practice. I would ask for the paid time and fees in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would travel affect the job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A setup job could be at several factories, so the posting must state the actual base and travel days. If the route keeps me from school pickup or cuts the mortgage wage, I wouldn't apply. A machine-setup title with no workable rota is no offer.

say: **2036 thinking AI** could plan orders before robots fill bottles around 2039.
A decade allows **real training checks** before changing jobs.
think: At **56**, the mortgage may still need my regular wage.
Our **four-month buffer** lets us check offers without assuming a permanent job.
do: **Save** new wages from full pay months after bills.
**Take** funded paid guarded setup training if a recognized place offered.
**Apply** for posted safe local setup jobs if qualified, hours shrink, pay and travel fit.
feel: **Uneasy** about later robots with secure wages today.
S4.quote: A machine-setup title with no workable rota is no offer.
fieldNote: She requests **written paid training** with guarded hands-on practice; an equipment-supplier enquiry alone is not enrolment.
The **setup application** needs qualification, reduced filling hours and a posted safe local role with sufficient pay and workable travel.

steps.text: Save new wages from full filling pay after bills
Ask supplier for written paid guarded setup training terms
Take recognized setup training if funded paid guarded place offered
Apply for posted safe local setup if qualified, hours shrink, pay and travel fit

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which worries you most, and what would help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The fast 2028 picture worries me most because capable robots around 2031 could cut the filling crew before a qualified job is ready. A written staffing plan, offered funded paid practical training and a posted safe local role at enough base pay would help. I'd check the school rota before taking any offer.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens after a robot signs off a capped soap bottle. A leak reaches a family's cupboard long after the line report says green.

headlineQuote: A leak reaches a family's cupboard long after the line report says green.
portrait: **Uma**, 43, operates a soap-bottle filling line with a vocational certificate and daily AI use for reject logs.
She and her bus-repair partner support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage, with four months saved and ordinary pay.
Her **centre outlook** leads her to compare real leak rates, wages and course terms before accepting claims.
Fast robots make her **alarmed** about a large crew cut; funded practical learning and safe posted local roles guide her plans.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring capable filling robots around 2031 before a qualified replacement job is ready.
whatWouldHelp: A **written staffing plan**, offered funded paid training and a posted safe local job at enough base pay would help.
